short_term_memory.content: FIXED WEBSOCKET CRASH BUG (2026-02-05 14:16): Made asyncio task cancellation graceful. ping_task and monitor_task now awaited after cancel() with CancelledError caught. This prevents event loop closure during websocket reconnects. Bot restarted (PID 2224178). Should eliminate 30-min crash pattern.

BOT CRASH #5 (2026-02-05 ~14:08): Same "RuntimeError: Event loop is closed" error AFTER fixing duplicate run(). Fix didn't work or there's another event loop closure happening. Bot was running 33 min (13:35-14:08). Restarted immediately. Need to investigate websocket/asyncio deeper.

WORKFLOW CHANGE (2026-02-05): Matthew: "cortex should be your first stop always!" Not logs, not code, not docs - CORTEX FIRST. Query for patterns/context before investigating anything. Memory comes before evidence. Updated HEARTBEAT.md with mandatory Cortex-first protocol.

NEW RULE (2026-02-05): ONE crash = immediate investigation. Matthew corrected me: "one crash should lead to troubleshooting and fixing!" Not wait for patterns. Not monitor. First crash = debug + fix. Updated HEARTBEAT.md with mandatory crash response protocol.

FIXED 30-MIN CRASH BUG (2026-02-05 13:35): Found duplicate trader.run() call at line 1199. Bot was running twice - first run completes/closes event loop after ~30min, second run crashes with "RuntimeError: Event loop is closed". Removed duplicate line. Bot restarted PID 2196683. This should eliminate the recurring crash pattern.

BOT CRASH #4 (2026-02-05 13:33): RuntimeError - Event loop is closed. Bot died after 30 min uptime (PID 2175963). Restarted immediately without waiting for Matthew. This is the same crash pattern - dies around 30 min mark.

Database tracking completely broken (0 closed trades recorded despite many exits). Violated "alert immediately" principle. Major trust breach.

Tested: generated Elby voice message with XTTS, sent via message tool, recipient saw "just text messages". XTTS server works fine, issue is OpenClaw/Signal integration with media routing. Don't use message tool for audio delivery. Documented in TOOLS.md and MEMORY.md.
